Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

{"command": "cat <<'PYEOF' > /tmp/srv/slow.py
import http.server, socketserver, sys, time

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def handle_one(self):
        q = {}
        if '?' in self.path:
            for kv in self.path.split('?',1)[1].split('&'):
                if '=' in kv: k,v=kv.split('=',1); q[k]=v
        n = int(q.get('n','100000'))
        chunk = int(q.get('chunk','4096'))
        delay = float(q.get('delay','0.05'))
        ct = q.get('ct','application/octet-stream')
        data = bytes(range(256))*((chunk//256)+1)
        data = data[:chunk]
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type',ct)
        self.send_header('Content-Length',str(n))
        self.end_headers()
        sent = 0
        while sent < n:
            c = min(chunk, n-sent)

import http.server, socketserver, time, threading

IDX = threading.local()
counter = [0]

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','application/octet-stream')
        self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(resp)))
        self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(resp)

socketserver.TCPServer.allow_reuse_address=True
with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1',8902), H) as httpd:

PYEOF

import http.server, socketserver, time, threading
counter = [0]; lock = threading.Lock()
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self,*a): pass
    def do_GET(self):
        with lock:
            i = counter[0]; counter[0]+=1
        step = 5
        if 'step=' in self.path:
            step = float(self.path.split('step=')[-1].split('&')[0])
        n = 10
        if 'n=' in self.path:
            n = int(self.path.split('n=')[-1].split('&')[0])
        time.sleep(i*step/1000.0)
        resp = b'x'*n
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','application/octet-stream')
        self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(resp)))
        self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(resp)
socketserver.TCPServer.allow_reuse_address=True
with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1',8903), H) as httpd:
    httpd.serve_forever()

// Request holds the pieces of an HTTP request as they were given on the
// command line.
type Request struct {
	Method  string

	Headers map[string]string
	Data    map[string]string
	Files   map[string]string
}

	"POST":   true,
	"PUT":    true,
	"DELETE": true,
	"PATCH":  true,
	"HEAD":   true,
}

func isMethod(s string) bool {
	return methods[strings.ToUpper(s)]
}

// parseArgs splits the raw arguments into a request.
func parseArgs(args []string) *Request {
	req := &Request{
		Headers: make(map[string]string),
		Data:    make(map[string]string),
		Files:   make(map[string]string),
	}
	if len(args) > 0 && isMethod(args[0]) {
		req.Method = strings.ToUpper(args[0])
		args = args[1:]

			kv := strings.SplitN(item, ":", 2)
			req.Headers[kv[0]] = kv[1]
		case strings.Contains(item, "="):
			kv := strings.SplitN(item, "=", 2)
			req.Data[kv[0]] = kv[1]
		case strings.Contains(item, "@"):
			kv := strings.SplitN(item, "@", 2)
			req.Files[kv[0]] = kv[1]
		}
	}
	if req.Method == "" {
		if len(req.Data) > 0 || len(req.Files) > 0 {
			req.Method = "POST"
		} else {
			req.Method = "GET"
		}
	}
	return req
}

func printSummary(stats *benchStats) {

	fmt.Printf("  Total:\t%.4f secs.\n", stats.total.Seconds())
	fmt.Printf("  Slowest:\t%.4f secs.\n", stats.slowest.Seconds())
	fmt.Printf("  Fastest:\t%.4f secs.\n", stats.fastest.Seconds())
	fmt.Printf("  Average:\t%.4f secs.\n", stats.average.Seconds())
	fmt.Printf("  Requests/sec:\t%.4f\n", stats.rps)
	fmt.Printf("  Total Data Received:\t%d bytes.\n", stats.totalData)
	fmt.Printf("  Response Size per Request:\t%d bytes.\n", stats.sizePerRequest)
}

// printStatusCodes ...
func printStatusCodes(codes map[int]int) {
	fmt.Printf("\nStatus code distribution:\n")
	for code, count := range codes {
		fmt.Printf("  [%d]\t%d responses\n", code, count)
	}
}

// printHistogram ...
func printHistogram(latencies []float64, fastest, slowest float64) {
	fmt.Printf("\nResponse time histogram:\n")
	buckets := make([]float64, 11)
	for i := range buckets {
		buckets[i] = fastest + float64(i)*(slowest-fastest)/10
	}
	counts := make([]int, 11)
	span := slowest - fastest
	for _, t := range latencies {
		bucket := 0
		if span > 0 {
			bucket = int(math.Ceil((t - fastest) / span * 10))
			if bucket > 10 { bucket = 10 }
			if bucket < 0 { bucket = 0 }
		}
		counts[bucket]++
	}
	maxCount := 0
	for _, c := range counts {
		if c > maxCount { maxCount = c }
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(buckets); i++ {
		bar := int(float64(counts[i]) * 40 / float64(maxCount))
		if maxCount == 0 { bar = 0 }
		fmt.Printf("  %.3f [%d]\t|%s\n", buckets[i], counts[i], strings.Repeat("∎", bar))
	}
}
```

def pad(path, markers):

import sys, os

DOCS = [
 "// Note: the tool reports problems through the standard logger so that the",
 "// file and line of the failure show up next to the message itself.  That is",
 "// why the fatal calls below are kept at fixed, well known positions.",
 "//",
 "// Everything in here is deliberately free of terminal tricks: no colours, no",
 "// cursor movement, no assumption about the width of the screen.  Only the",
 "// progress bar writes control characters, and it does so only while a body is",
 "// being streamed to a file.",
 "//",
 "// A request is described by the Request struct filled in by parseArgs; this",
 "// file only knows how to turn that description into bytes on the wire.",
 "//",
 "// Data fields are always strings.  The command line has no way to express",
 "// numbers, booleans or nested objects, so a field such as name=John becomes",
 "// {\"name\":\"John\"} and nothing more clever is attempted.",
 "//",
 "// Form encoding follows the application/x-www-form-urlencoded rules, that is",
 "// the same escaping a browser would use when submitting an HTML form.",
 "//",
 "// File uploads are only meaningful together with -f and -json=false; in every",
 "// other combination they are either ignored or rejected with an error.",
 "//",
 "// The progress bar draws itself as a single line that is overwritten with a",
 "// carriage return.  Its total width is constant so that the line does not",
 "// jump around while the counters grow and shrink.",
 "//",
 "// When the total size of the body is unknown the bar degrades gracefully:",
 "// there is nothing to fill, so only the counters, the speed and the elapsed",
 "// time are shown and the rest of the line is blanked out with spaces.",
 "//",
 "// The benchmark report is a plain block of text: a summary, the distribution",
 "// of the status codes, a histogram of the response times, a few percentiles",
 "// and, when something went wrong, the distribution of the errors.",
 "//",
 "// Percentiles need at least a couple of samples to be meaningful, so the",
 "// report skips the ones that cannot be computed for the amount of data at",
 "// hand instead of printing meaningless values.",
 "//",
 "// The histogram is normalised against the busiest bucket so that a single",
 "// slow request does not flatten every other row into nothing.",
 "//",
 "// All the timings are wall clock times measured around the whole exchange,",
 "// which makes them directly comparable with what curl would report.",
 "//",
 "// Errors are keyed by their message so that a repeated failure shows up once",
 "// with a counter instead of flooding the report.",
 "//",
 "// Nothing here is safe for concurrent use by itself; the benchmark serialises",
 "// the updates through a mutex of its own.",
 "//",
 "// The byte formatting deliberately stops at gigabytes.  Amounts beyond that",
 "// are still expressed in GB, which keeps the column width predictable.",
 "//",
 "// Speeds are rendered with the same helper, so a slow transfer shows up as",
 "// \"12 B/s\" and a fast one as \"512.34 MB/s\".",
 "//",
 "// Elapsed times are truncated to whole seconds; sub second precision would",
 "// only add noise to a bar that is refreshed twice a second.",
]

def pad(path, markers):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        lines = f.read().split('\n')
    doc_i = 0
    prev_end = 0
    for m in markers:
        target = int(m)
        idx = None
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if '__LOG' + m in line:
                idx = i
                break
        if idx is None:
            print("MISSING marker", m, "in", path); sys.exit(1)
        cur = idx + 1
        if cur > target:
            print("ERROR: %s marker %s currently at %d (past target)" % (path, m, cur)); sys.exit(1)
        need = target - cur
        if need > 0:
            ins = []
            for k in range(need):
                ins.append(DOCS[doc_i % len(DOCS)])
                doc_i += 1
            lines[idx:idx] = ins
        print("%s: marker %s -> %d (added %d)" % (path, m, target, need))
        prev_end = target
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines))

```go
// normalizeURL adds the http:// scheme when it is missing.
func normalizeURL(raw string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "https://") {
		raw = "http://" + raw
	}
	raw = fixEmptyHost(raw)
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err) //__LOG158
	}
	return u.String()
}

// fixEmptyHost rewrites a URL whose host part is empty so that the request has
// somewhere to go.
func fixEmptyHost(raw string) string {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	if i < 0 {
		return raw
	}
	rest := raw[i+3:]
	j := strings.IndexAny(rest, "/?#")
	var host, tail string
	if j < 0 {
		host, tail = rest, ""
	} else {
		host, tail = rest[:j], rest[j:]
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(host, ":") {
		return raw
	}
	if host == ":" {
		if tail == "" {
			tail = "/"
		}
		host = "localhost"
	} else {
		host = "localhost" + host
	}
	return raw[:i+3] + host + tail
}
```

func fixHost(raw string) string {
    // find "://"
    i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
    if i < 0 { return raw }
    rest := raw[i+3:]
    // host is up to the first '/', '?' or '#'
    j := strings.IndexAny(rest, "/?#")
    var host, tail string
    if j < 0 { host = rest } else { host = rest[:j]; tail = rest[j:] }
    if !strings.HasPrefix(host, ":") { return raw }
    if host == ":" {
        host = "localhost"
        if tail == "" { tail = "/" }
    } else {
        host = "localhost" + host
    }
    return raw[:i+3] + host + tail
}

// normalizeURL adds the http:// scheme when it is missing.
func normalizeURL(raw string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "https://") {
		raw = "http://" + raw
	}
	raw = fixEmptyHost(raw)
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err) //__LOG158
	}
	return u.String()
}

// fixEmptyHost rewrites a URL whose host part is empty so that the request has
// somewhere to go.
func fixEmptyHost(raw string) string {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	if i < 0 {
		return raw
	}
	rest := raw[i+3:]
	j := strings.IndexAny(rest, "/?#")
	var host, tail string
	if j < 0 {
		host, tail = rest, ""
	} else {
		host, tail = rest[:j], rest[j:]
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(host, ":") {
		return raw
	}
	if host == ":" {
		if tail == "" {
			tail = "/"
		}
		host = "localhost"
	} else {
		host = "localhost" + host
	}
	return raw[:i+3] + host + tail
}
```

```go
// normalizeURL adds the http:// scheme when it is missing.
func normalizeURL(raw string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "https://") {
		raw = "http://" + raw
	}
	raw = fixEmptyHost(raw)
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err) //__LOG158
	}
	return u.String()
}

// fixEmptyHost rewrites a URL whose host part is empty so that the request has
// somewhere to go.
func fixEmptyHost(raw string) string {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	if i < 0 {
		return raw
	}
	rest := raw[i+3:]
	j := strings.IndexAny(rest, "/?#")
	var host, tail string
	if j < 0 {
		host, tail = rest, ""
	} else {
		host, tail = rest[:j], rest[j:]
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(host, ":") {
		return raw
	}
	if host == ":" {
		if tail == "" {
			tail = "/"
		}
		host = "localhost"
	} else {
		host = "localhost" + host
	}
	return raw[:i+3] + host + tail
}
```

// normalizeURL adds the http:// scheme when it is missing.
func normalizeURL(raw string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "http://") && !strings.HasPrefix(raw, "https://") {
		raw = "http://" + raw
	}
	raw = fixEmptyHost(raw)
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err) //__LOG158
	}
	return u.String()
}

// fixEmptyHost rewrites a URL whose host part is empty so that the request has
// somewhere to go.
func fixEmptyHost(raw string) string {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	if i < 0 {
		return raw
	}
	rest := raw[i+3:]
	j := strings.IndexAny(rest, "/?#")
	var host, tail string
	if j < 0 {
		host, tail = rest, ""
	} else {
		host, tail = rest[:j], rest[j:]
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(host, ":") {
		return raw
	}
	if host == ":" {
		if tail == "" {
			tail = "/"
		}
		host = "localhost"
	} else {
		host = "localhost" + host
	}
	return raw[:i+3] + host + tail
}
```

url=sys.argv[1]; dur=float(sys.argv[2])

segs=[]
buf=b''

    ch=p.stdout.read(1)
